$comment: INFERRED AGGREGATE TIER — the Requirements Synthesizer's reduce output, and the direct backing for requirement.md. Two rules: (1) all prose is stored FINISHED, so rendering requirement.md is deterministic assembly rather than a second LLM pass — the md can then never contradict the JSON; (2) every entry cites `evidence` ids that must exist in signature/dependencies/functions/template.json, validated mechanically. Dangling evidence is a hard failure, not a warning. Strict JSON; annotations use $comment keys.

rendersTo.$comment: Section mapping consumed by the requirement.md renderer.

purpose.statement: <one to three sentences: what this unit exists to do, in domain language>

external.name: <name>
external.description: <what it holds and who mutates it>

propsAndEvents.description: <what the parent passes, or what the parent should do on this event>

publicContract.$comment: requirement.md §4 — the ADT view. Consumer's point of view, restating signature.json.publicApi as intent.

methods.contract: <what it guarantees to do for a caller>

inputContracts.meaning: <what the parent is expected to pass>

outputContracts.meaning: <what the parent should do on this event>

workflows.$comment: requirement.md §3/§4 — behavior reconstructed from the ordered function explanations.
workflows.name: <Save an edited record>
workflows.trigger: <user submits the form | ngOnInit | parent changes input X>

lifecycleBehavior.$comment: requirement.md §2/§3 — ordering matters and is a classic migration hazard.
lifecycleBehavior.onInitialization: <what happens when the unit is created>

behavioralInvariants.$comment: The migration's real acceptance bar: things that must remain true regardless of implementation.

acceptanceCriteria.$comment: requirement.md §6 — stored structured, not only as prose, so a testing agent can consume it directly. Derived from workflows, invariants, and existing spec cases.

domainRules.$comment: requirement.md §7 — for SME review. This section is the most likely to be human-edited, so the renderer must treat it as human-owned once touched.

migration.$comment: Renders to migration_notes.md, NOT requirement.md — this keeps requirement.md framework-neutral and reviewable by SMEs who do not know the target framework. Name the Angular assumption at risk; leave target-framework design to Stage 2.

risks.category: <rxjs-pipeline | mutable-service-state | direct-dom-access | lifecycle-ordering | di-assumption | change-detection | forms-semantics | style-encapsulation | template-directive | routing | third-party-dependency | subscription-leak | security>
risks.description: <the Angular-specific behavior that will not carry over verbatim>
risks.behaviorAtRisk: <the observable behavior that could silently change>

review.$comment: The human gate. Stage 2 must not begin while status is 'pending' or any blocking question is open.

suspectedDefects.description: <apparent bug in the existing Angular code>

unresolvedReferences: <symbol or selector that could not be linked to a unit>

humanOwnedSections.$comment: Populated by the renderer when it detects a human edit (section hash mismatch). Listed sections are never overwritten on regeneration.

provenance.inputHash: <hash of the ast tiers + synthesizerVersion; the cache key>
